IT IS COMMITTED ON PURPOSE. The prior art (cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.mjs) was
credited by D111 as 'mutation-proven in BOTH directions with working --ledger fixture injection',
and that credential is NOT RE-DERIVABLE FROM MAIN: `git grep -ln defectCommits` returns exactly one
tracked file, the module itself, and no tracked JSON carries its fixture keys. The fixture was a
throwaway and the proof evaporated on merge. This one does not.
WHAT A GREEN HERE IS NOT. Under --ledger the command reads NOTHING live: it never walks the task
corpus, never calls `bp task ready`, and never issues the pinned filter[parent_id] query. Clauses
(b), (b') and (c) are read straight off the rows below. This is the exact shape of the trap in the
prior art, where clause (b) under --ledger reads `fixture.landed` and NEVER shells to
`git merge-base`. So a green here is a MUTATION CONTROL — proof the command is ABLE TO PASS — and
never evidence about the live ledger, whose only honest reading is a live run.
WHAT IS STILL REAL HERE. Clause (a) is NOT stubbed. The reruns below are executed through the real
screenedRerun path, so the D50 absence veto is live in this proof. A hand-built result would make it
silently absent: admitsAbsenceClaim({verdict:'FAILED'}) with no absenceEligible key returns TRUE.
